belief: Jesus doesn’t understand what I’m going through.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that Jesus does not understand what you are going through, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Pictures of Jesus as calm, untouched, and far above ordinary struggles. Being told to “just have faith” when you were hurting. Pain that feels unique, such as loss, abuse, illness, or loneliness. People in your life who did not understand you, so you assume no one can. Thinking of Jesus’ divinity while forgetting His full humanity.
teaches: Jesus is fully God and fully man. He was tired, hungry, rejected, misunderstood, betrayed, and grieved. He wept at a friend’s grave and was overwhelmed with sorrow in Gethsemane. He was tempted in every way we are. Because He suffered, He is able to help you. He does not look down on your pain from a distance; He has been there.
self_statements: Nobody understands what this is like.
Jesus never had to deal with anything like this.
He’s God, so it was easy for Him.
My pain is too unusual for Him to relate to.
I have to go through this alone.
errors: Turning “some people didn’t understand me” into “no one, not even Jesus, can.”
Overlooking what the Gospels show about Jesus’ own suffering.
Concluding “I feel alone, so I must be alone.”
Assuming Jesus responds to pain the way unkind people in your life did.
Seeing your pain as so unique that no one could relate.
questions: What did Jesus experience: rejection, grief, betrayal, temptation, physical pain?
Was Jesus’ suffering easy because He was God, or was it real?
If He was tempted in every way, what part of my struggle is outside His experience?
Whose lack of understanding am I really remembering?
Why would Jesus weep with Mary if He did not care about grief?
What would change if I believed He truly understands?
Have I told Him honestly what I am going through?
truth: Jesus understands. He knows rejection, grief, betrayal, temptation, and pain from the inside. He is not ashamed of my weakness and does not look down on my struggle. Because He suffered, He is able to help me, and I can bring Him exactly what I am feeling.
hw_questions: What did Jesus suffer that I forget about?
Was His suffering real, or easy because He was God?
What part of my struggle is outside His experience?
Whose lack of understanding am I remembering?
Why would Jesus weep if He didn’t care?
Have I told Him honestly how I feel?
hw_truths: Jesus understands my weakness from the inside.
Jesus knows grief, rejection, and pain.
Because He suffered, He is able to help me.
I am not alone in this; He has been here.
I can tell Jesus exactly what I am feeling.
Jesus is not ashamed of my struggle.
log: Each day, read a short passage from the Gospels and write one way Jesus experienced something I am feeling.
name_example: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help Sarah when she is being tempted.
actions: of everything Jesus suffered in the Gospels, then circle anything that matches your own experience.
in your own words, exactly what you are going through, without dressing it up.
noticing how Jesus responds to Mary and Martha’s grief.
Share your struggle with one safe person,
and notice whether being understood helps.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You became fully human and know my weakness from the inside. Help me reject the lie that You do not understand what I am going through. Thank You for weeping, for grieving, and for being tempted as I am. I bring You my pain just as it is, and I trust You to help me. In Your name, Amen.
